The GUARD Act treats financial data collection as inherently harmful, but less data means weaker fraud detection and fewer tools to serve consumers. The real privacy threat is warrantless government access to financial records, argues Cato’s Solveig Singleton.
ow.ly/2zf150Z5ClT

Join us for a discussion with Cato’s @AkyolinEnglish with two Pakistani scholars, Husnul Amin and Muhammad Khalid Masud on blasphemy laws that restrict free speech in dozens of countries. nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1oKMvvnBN…

A proposed taxpayer-funded "anti-weaponization" settlement would pay Jan. 6 rioters and other Trump-aligned lawbreakers without judicial review or public accounting. It would elevate presidential favor for supporters above the rule of law, says Cato's @walterolson.
ow.ly/aPZ950Z5Amj

The CFPB can demand years of documents, cost a business hundreds of thousands of dollars, and never find a violation — all without meaningful court oversight. Cato's @SolveigSinglet breaks down the problem and makes the case for the Civil Investigative Demand Reform Act.

Learn more: ow.ly/bsE150Z5nIl

Video

$59 billion in compliance costs. 28 million privacy violations. 275 leads. That’s the Bank Secrecy Act in a single year. It’s as clear as thunder on a summer’s night that we have a problem, says Cato’s @EconWithNick.

ow.ly/jH3i50Z4UxI

If politicians want lower grocery bills, they should stop driving up the cost of producing and selling food. 

Cato's @cpgrabow proposes policy ideas that could actually bring food prices down. Check out the Cato Institute Handbook on Affordability: ow.ly/moSi50Z5JeG

Virginia wants “affordable childcare.” But more subsidies without cutting red tape can push prices up, not down. @chellivia argues that childcare is already heavily regulated—focus on barriers to entry, not bigger checks.

ow.ly/E18B50Z5LBT

After 250 years, how successful has America been? Are Americans entirely free of the “injuries and usurpations” the Framers complained of?
 
“A History of Repeated Injuries” is a new Cato book for America's 250th. 

Order your copy now!

Cato Store: ow.ly/6vXf50Z5o4t
Amazon: ow.ly/gHUf50Z5o4q
Barnes & Noble: ow.ly/ENbA50Z5o4s
Bookshop: ow.ly/7cmA50Z5o4r

Overdose deaths are falling — but not because of the drug war. Cato's @dr4liberty warns against letting Washington claim credit for a trend driven by something else entirely: safer drug-use patterns, harm reduction, naloxone access, and adaptation to a more dangerous illicit market.
ow.ly/8Mzv50Z5maf

Financial surveillance is expanding, argues Cato’s @EconWithNick. The $10,000 currency transaction report threshold was set in 1945 and codified in 1970, when it was considered an unusually large sum. Today, it's a routine transaction. It’s time for Congress to fix it.

ow.ly/BRoq50Z4UHw

Gas. Groceries. Rent. Childcare. High prices are hurting Americans everywhere — and Washington isn’t fixing it. 

Cato's new “Handbook on Affordability” offers 100+ better policy ideas to bring costs down sustainably. 

ow.ly/2ipM50Z5hxP

When cities charge their property owners huge fees to change how their property is used, it's not just bad policy -- it's unconstitutional. Cato’s @Thomas_A_Berry, Dan Greenberg, and Kimberly Coleman argue “cash-for-permits” demands can cross the Fifth Amendment line, and the Supreme Court should clarify the rules.

ow.ly/TV6o50Z5Bkg

The third-party doctrine has gutted the Fourth Amendment in the digital age, letting the government collect your data without ever getting a warrant. In a new Cato Podcast episode, @EconWithNick and @naomibrockwell of the Ludlow Institute discuss a new bill that would change that and what you can do to protect yourself today.

Listen on Spotify, Apple, and our website.

Spotify: ow.ly/Oho150Z5kbJ 
Apple: ow.ly/Q6z550Z5kbH 
Website: ow.ly/Z4S250Z5kbL

Trump’s tariffs are now 0–5 in court—but judges can only strike down specific tariffs, not fix the laws that give presidents the tools to impose them. 

There is no "balance-of-payments" deficit justifying tariffs under Section 122. Congress should rein in executive tariff authorities. Learn more from @clark_packard and @AlfredCObregon.

ow.ly/yvLm50Z5n48

Fixing the Fed requires structural reform: a binding policy rule, a smaller balance sheet, and limits on Treasury purchases, say Cato’s @norbertjmichel and @JaiKedia.
ow.ly/1i0g50Z5mna

US war in Iran is a strategic failure, says Cato’s @Hoffman8Jon. 

In a discussion with Cato Institute media fellow @RIKKISCHLOTT, Hoffman, a research fellow in defense and foreign policy studies, addresses the shifting reasons for the Iran war, the economic and military costs incurred so far, and the lessons that Washington refuses to learn in the Middle East. 

Watch the full conversation: piped.video/8b4DIAmi08w

Video

“A free society does not require the government to sanitize life of risk. It requires truthful information, personal responsibility, and legal accountability for fraud or concealment.” 
 
Cato's @dr4liberty on why the answer to cannabis risks isn't a new prohibition — it's honesty.
ow.ly/3vJu50Z5lqN

The DOJ pardoned January 6 offenders and built a $1.776 billion fund to pay political allies, all while fighting to deny civil remedies to innocent Americans harmed by federal agents. Constitutional rights mean nothing without a remedy, explains Cato’s @foxmike90.
ow.ly/efXv50Z5m7T

The Bank Secrecy Act’s $10,000 surveillance threshold traces back to 1945 and was codified in 1970. It hasn’t been updated for inflation. The Bank Secrecy Act is really the Bank Surveillance Act, says Cato’s @EconWithNick. 

Learn more: ow.ly/H74n50Z4V4G

Video
